long_biography.plain_text:
Saudi lawyer Ahmed Zaki Yamani grew up among scholars: his father and grandfather were judges, and he initially wanted to teach. His concern for endangered books later took institutional form in Al-Furqan, the foundation he established and sponsored in London. Its work addressed manuscripts threatened by conflict, neglect and inadequate preservation resources.

The foundation commissioned a worldwide survey of Islamic manuscript collections, bringing together specialists to document holdings in public and private libraries. The resulting reference work covered 106 countries and identified both published catalogues and previously unpublished lists. Alongside this collective effort, Yamani wrote a detailed historical study of Khadija's house in Mecca, examining its location and architecture.
